outline.description: This chapter establishes the governing legal rules, including the standard of review for indictment sufficiency and the elements of the securities fraud statute. It introduces the relevant Supreme Court precedents that frame the legal analysis.

outline.chapter_title: The Scheme to Defraud and Property Interest Requirement
outline.description: This chapter analyzes the first major legal hurdle: whether the indictment alleges a deprivation of a protected property interest. It distinguishes between the rejected 'right-to-control' theory and the accepted 'fraudulent-inducement' theory in light of Ciminelli.
subtopics: The Defendants' Argument Regarding Economic Information vs. Property
Supreme Court Holding in Ciminelli v. United States

Why the Indictment Alleges Deprivation of Money or Property

outline.chapter_title: The Intent to Defraud and Economic Harm Requirement
outline.description: This chapter examines the second major legal hurdle: whether the indictment sufficiently alleges the requisite intent to defraud. It addresses the argument that intent to profit without intent to cause net economic loss is insufficient, applying Kousisis.
subtopics: Elements of Intent to Defraud: Deception and Harm
The Defendants' Argument Regarding Profit vs. Victim Harm
Supreme Court Holding in Kousisis v. United States
Rejection of the Requirement for Net Pecuniary Loss
Sufficiency of Alleging Intent to Obtain Money via Deception
